title: Ephemeral headroom reconciliation and per-request rate smoothing for dedicated pools
creator: Asha Balan
description:
Summary: Implement an event-sourced reconciliation layer that converts short-lived 'ephemeral headroom' allocations into time-normalised usage records and issues retroactive micro-credits when reserved capacity transiently under-delivers. This work targets dedicated GPU pools where we currently see transient throttling and burst drops that are not reconciled granularly, leading to customer disputes and opaque billing adjustments.

Problem statement: Dedicated pools offer reserved throughput and configurable burst headroom. Under transient load spikes and hardware hiccups we observe: 1) brief per-tenant throttles that are currently reconciled at coarse 5-15 minute windows, 2) imprecise attribution of micro-bursts across tenants sharing a pool, and 3) manual sla-credit workflows for customers with measurable SLA violations. These lead to delayed credits, poor auditability, and edge-case double-billing/negative-balance spikes.

Goals:
- Provide sub-second accounting of ephemeral headroom allocations and consumptions.
- Smooth per-request rate calculations so that short-lived spikes do not unfairly exhaust reserved quotas.
- Automatically generate retroactive credits (micro-credits) when dedicated pool metrics show sustained under-delivery vs committed throughput over a configurable amortization window.
- Maintain an auditable event log per tenant with immutable ledger entries for all allocation, consumption, and credit events.

Non-goals:
- Replace high-level SLA policy definitions (we will consume existing SLA configs).
- Tackle cross-pool burst-shaping in this ticket (follow-on work).

Key concepts and terms introduced:
- Ephemeral headroom: transient capacity made available to tenants when pool utilization < 100% (sub-second granularity).
- Micro-credit: fractional SLA credit units (e.g. 0.0001 throughput-seconds) that represent small compensatory adjustments.
- Time-weighted smoothing: a sliding-window exponential smoothing applied to per-tenant request rates to avoid short spikes draining quotas.
- Event types: ALLOCATION, CONSUMPTION, ALLOC_RELEASE, ADJUSTMENT, CREDIT_ISSUED, RECONCILIATION_RUN.

High-level design:
1) Runtime emits fine-grained events for every allocation and consumption with a unique request fingerprint and tenant id. Events are buffered in a regionally redundant event-stream (Kafka).
2) A reconcilier service consumes events and performs per-tenant rolling aggregation at 1s granularity, computing a smoothed usage delta and detecting under-delivery windows by comparing committed throughput to observed served tokens.
3) When an under-delivery is detected above a threshold for a tenant, the reconcilier creates CREDIT_ISSUED ledger events, storing them in the tenant ledger table and sending a notification to the billing pipeline.
4) Backfill and retroactive adjustments: the reconcilier can re-run over historical segments (bounded by retention) to compute missed credits and mark them with backfill metadata.
5) UI/Console: Expose a per-tenant micro-credit ledger view and a dispute initiation flow; include links to raw event segments for audit.

Storage & schema notes (high-level):
- ledger_entries (tenant_id, seq_id, event_type, amount_str, timestamp_iso, request_fp, source_run_id, note). All fields stored as strings in this ticket's artifacts.
- retention: primary event store 14 days hot, 90 days warm; ledger entries persisted for billing retention term.

Operational constraints:
- The reconcilier must operate within a bounded memory footprint per consumer partition; aggregation uses fixed-size ring buffers for 1s buckets.
- Avoid introducing per-request RPCs to the billing DB; use append-only writes to the ledger with idempotency keys derived from request_fp+event_ts.

Telemetry and metrics:
- new metrics: dedicated.pool.ephemeral_headroom.alloc_rate, .consumption_rate, .smoothed_rate, .underdelivery_seconds, .microcredits_issued_count, .microcredits_issued_total_amount.
- alerts: underdelivery_seconds > 120 (per tenant) => paging on-call SRE; backlog of unprocessed events > 300k => operational alert.

API and billing pipeline changes:
- Billing ingestion accepts micro-credits in the same batch format as existing credits but with a micro_credit flag.
- Console exposes a 'micro-credit ledger' export (CSV) and a filtered view for reconstructions.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- New ledger table will be additive. Existing invoices are unaffected until a micro-credit batch runs.
- Reconciler will have a dry-run mode to generate credits internally without sending them to billing for 2 weeks for validation.

Acceptance Criteria (see separate field): Describes observable success criteria and how to validate in staging and prod.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler consumes runtime events and produces smoothed per-tenant rates at 1s granularity in staging.
Dry-run micro-credit reports match manual reference implementation within 0.1% for three sampled pools.
Issuing micro-credits to billing pipeline succeeds with idempotency and no invoice regressions in prod-like environment.
Console shows per-tenant ledger entries with linkable event segments and supports dispute initiation flow.
Automated tests for idempotency, replay safety, and retention enforcement included in CI.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for smoothing and credit calculation (edge cases: request_fp collisions, clock skew). 2) Integration in staging: enable reconcilier in dry-run for three dedicated pools for 14 days, compare outputs to canonical offline calculation. 3) Canary: enable credits_publish=false in prod for one small pool and run scheduled reconciliations. 4) Gradual publish: enable credits_publish for 1% of tenants, inspect invoices and ledger exports. 5) Audit: independent finance validation of micro-credit batches before broad rollout.
rollback_plan: Reconciler runs are idempotent and credit publishes are gated. If we observe invoice regressions or ledger corruption, disable the publisher flag, revert the last credit batch by issuing a corrective adjustment entry (ADJUSTMENT with negative amount), and restore from last known-good ledger snapshot. Communication plan: notify finance and SRE channels and pause auto-credits for 24h while investigating.
comments: 2025-01-10 - Asha Balan: Ticket created after recurring customer complaint about unclear credits for brief throttles. Collected initial traces from pool 'eu-west-1-pool-3'.
2025-01-15 - Miguel Ortega: Spike attribution PoC completed. We can generate per-request fingerprints using consistent hashing of tenant+route+trace_id; initial collision rate < 1e-8.
2025-01-20 - Priya Sharma (Finance): Requested that micro-credits be represented as separate line-items in exports and flagged 'micro_credit' for downstream tooling. Also requested dry-run period.
2025-01-28 - Evan Park (SRE): Identified potential hot-partition risk for pools with >1k tenants; proposed sharding by tenant_id mod 64 and backpressure on consumer lag.
2025-02-03 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented smoothing prototype (alpha=0.4) and validated in staging traces; initial results show 45% reduction in false-positive quota drains on synthetic bursts.
2025-02-10 - Design review: Console micro-ledger mockups approved; added 'dispute' button with pre-populated event context. UX notes linked in attachments.
2025-02-12 - Miguel Ortega: Reconcilier dry-run started for two small pools; publishing disabled. Monitoring dashboards instrumented and baseline exported to drive.
implementation_notes: Idempotency: use composite idempotency key = sha256(request_fp + event_ts + run_id). Replayer: supports bounds by event offset and time window. Performance: prefer append-only bulk writes to ledger with batched 1s groups. Use circuit-breaker when consumer lag > 250k events.
ledger_schema_migration: Add ledger_entries table (append-only) with columns: tenant_id (string), seq_id (string), event_type (string), amount_str (string), timestamp_iso (string), request_fp (string), source_run_id (string), note (string). Populate sequences using monotonic seq_id prefixed by tenant_id. Backfill path: offline job converts historical aggregated windows into CREDIT_ISSUED rows for last 90 days.

Implement reconcilier core processing loop and smoothing functions (by 2025-01-31).

Iterate on console micro-ledger UI and link to dispute workflow (by 2025-02-21).
